text:
Toronto trailed 3-0 in the second period and still won, because the game was never as lopsided as that scoreboard made it look. NSH built the lead in the first period, out-chancing TOR 2.52 to 1.02 in expected goals, with Steven Stamkos scoring on the power play and Nils Hoglander adding two backhanders, one in each of the first two periods. After that, the chances belonged almost entirely to TOR. In each of the last three periods the home team had the better of the expected goals, and the TOR shot attempts finished 72 to 52.

The comeback came in a hurry. John Tavares scored on a 4% chance at 4:56 of the second, and William Nylander cut it to one on the power play two minutes later. Stamkos restored the two-goal lead with a 3% look, but Gavin McKenna answered a minute later. Jack Roslovic tied it at 4 in the third, and the shot count showed why: TOR put 37 on goal to NSH's 25, and Juuse Saros allowed 4.42 expected goals' worth of chances and gave up five.

Auston Matthews ended it in overtime, set up by Nylander, who also had a hand in the tying goal. Matthews finished with a goal and three assists while TOR created 2.67 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.78 allowed. By expected goals, TOR deserved to win 56% of the time, a thin edge that still beat a night when Anthony Stolarz stopped almost exactly what the chances suggested.
